items.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023
items.q: Miles did not touch me like Clifford did or Lee Morgan or Kenny Dorham, players like Charlie Shavers

ctx.x: Oh yeah, oh yeah I sure did. I’ve got a couple of stories about that too, I don’t know — well yeah, I could tell you, I could tell you, beautiful. We were at Universal, we had a nine in the morning call and there was a double session and it was a Monday. And we called him “The Creeper.” Jack was The Creeper. And the reason he was called The Creeper was cause he’d creep in and then he’d creep out. And so we’re doing this nine in the morning double session at Universal and the contractor’s name was Bobby Helfer.…

how you had to be an individual. How you had to create your own sound. That’s the case with me and the people that I worked with back in the day. When you heard Conrad Gozzo playing lead you knew it was Conrad Gozzo you know. When you heard Conte Candoli playing a solo, you knew it was Conte Candoli. You heard Pete Candoli you knew it was Pete Candoli. You know it’s just — Plas Johnson, you knew it was Plas Johnson. I listened to everybody and I picked up everybody from playing records and records and sitting…

Do you have a sense — I’m going to refer back to that “Nature Boy” recording because there’s some pretty sophisticated orchestrations behind you. Do you have the kind of ear and chordal knowledge that you know what those chords are when you’re improvising over them?
